new_entities.name: Juice-cleansing protocols
new_entities.description: Short-term juice-only or juice-dominant dietary regimens promoted for cleansing, reset, or metabolic improvement.

new_entities.name: Metabolic outcomes
new_entities.description: Outcomes related to weight, glucose regulation, lipid status, inflammation, or other metabolic-health markers.

edges.effect_quant: The direct cleanse literature is sparse and small. A six-person juice-fasting feasibility study mainly described microbiome shifts rather than clear metabolic benefit, while a 14-person intervention study found that short-term exclusive juice intake was associated with microbiome changes that could plausibly be metabolically unfavorable because of high sugar and low fiber exposure. Adjacent vegetable-juice interventions can improve some metabolic-syndrome components, but that does not validate short-term juice cleanses as a distinct metabolic therapy.
edges.population: healthy adults or overweight adults using short-term juice-only or juice-dominant dietary interventions
edges.mechanism: Juice cleanses sharply reduce insoluble fiber while concentrating rapidly absorbable sugars and phytochemicals, which may cause transient caloric restriction effects but also microbiome and glycemic tradeoffs.
edges.summary: This is a contested metabolic-health edge. Juice cleanses can change intake patterns quickly, but the direct human evidence is too small and inconsistent to support broad claims of meaningful metabolic reset or detoxification.
edges.caveats: Evidence from vegetable-juice supplementation or polyphenol-rich juice trials should not be casually generalized to multi-day juice-only cleanses. The cleanse-specific literature remains tiny and methodologically weak.
